overview: Ebola disease is a severe, often fatal illness in humans caused by viruses that belong to the Orthoebolavirus genus of the filoviridae family. It is often fatal and has a case fatality rate of around 50%. Early intensive supportive care with rehydration and treatment of symptoms improves survival.
diagnosis: reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) assay
transmission: contact with contaminated objects or surfaces
close contact with patients without infection control precautions
burial ceremonies with direct contact with the body of a person who has died
risk_factors: people in close contact with infected animals
people in close contact with infected people
key_facts: The average Ebola disease case fatality rate is around 50%
Case fatality rates have varied from 25–90% in past outbreaks
